The Modupe Adelabu Political Family, a group led by former Ekiti State Deputy Governor, Prof Modupe Adelabu, has expressed readiness to mobilise across the 16 local government areas of the state for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima. The group, in a statement made available to PUNCH on Sunday, stated that it would flag off the Tinubu-Shettima re-election rally on Thursday at a grand event billed for the Mini Pavilion, Fajuyi, Ado-Ekiti, the Ekiti State capital. It said the event, which would be hosted by Adelabu, who is the Governing Board Chairman of the National Examinations Council, “is aimed at demonstrating political unity, grassroots mobilisation and commitment to the Tinubu-Shettima re-election project ahead of the 2027 general election. “It will have in attendance Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, as chief host and former Governor Segun Oni as the special guest of honour. The Deputy Governor, Mrs Monisade Afuye, will serve as the Mother of the Day, while Otunba Ladi Owolabi is Chairman of the Planning Committee. “The flag-off ceremony is expected to bring together political stakeholders, party loyalists and supporters of the President and Vice-President in Ekiti State,” the group stated. Tinubu approves N1.5tn recapitalisation of BOA Ex-NDC spokesman Abdulsalami defects to Atiku’s ADC ADC crisis: Gombe mocks Atiku as feud deepens According to the organisers, the gathering will provide a platform for members and supporters of the political family to reaffirm their support for the Renewed Hope Agenda and strengthen their mobilisation efforts towards the 2027 elections. They described the ceremony as “a significant step in consolidating the political structure of the Adelabu family across the state, with representatives from the 16 local government areas expected to participate.” The political family, while declaring its readiness to rally behind the Tinubu-Shettima re-election bid, said, “The gathering is a demonstration of unity and commitment to the administration’s political aspirations”. Abiodun Nejo
